title: Each tab saves its own stale in-memory list over the shared one, so a second tab erases the first tab's recipes
evidence: recipes is read from localStorage once at startup (app.js:3). saveRecipes writes the whole array (store.js:15). There is no `storage` event handler and no re-read before the write. Driven with two pages in one browser context.
failing_case: Open the app in tabs A and B. Add 'Soup' in A. Add 'Pie' in B. localStorage.recipes is then only [Pie]. 'Soup' is lost after any reload.
remediation: Re-read the stored list immediately before each write and merge by id, and listen to the `storage` event to refresh the view. Or take a lock for the read-modify-write.

quote: return [];  // storage blocked or corrupt: start empty; app.js tells the user
title: Corrupt or old-shape saved data is silently shown as empty, then overwritten by the next add; the comment's promise is false
evidence: app.js never reads a load failure and sets no message at startup (statusEl is only written in the two handlers). Driven: localStorage.recipes = truncated JSON gives 'No recipes yet. Add your first one above.' and an empty status. Adding one recipe then leaves localStorage.recipes as only the new record. The filter at store.js:7 also silently drops any record without a string name, and the next save permanently removes it.
failing_case: A previous version stored [{"title":"Pie","mins":30}], or a write was cut off. The user sees an empty list with no warning, adds one recipe, and the original raw data is gone for good.
remediation: Have loadRecipes return {list, problem}. When parsing fails or records are dropped, keep the raw string under a backup key, tell the user in the status region, and put a version on the saved shape with a migration.

title: parseInt truncates valid type=number input such as 1e2 to 1, silently saving the wrong time
evidence: Driven: the #minutes input accepts '1e2' (checkValidity() true; it is within min 1, max 600). The handler saved and announced 'E 1 min', 'Total cooking time: 1 minutes.'
failing_case: The user types 1e2 (or 6e1) in Minutes and presses Save. The app stores 1 and says Saved, with no sign anything was altered.
remediation: Read input.valueAsNumber (or Number(value)) and require Number.isInteger and the min/max range, so the JS check matches the HTML constraint.

title: Delete ignores a failed save and still reports "Deleted"
evidence: saveRecipes returns false on a storage error (store.js:13-20). The add handler checks that result (app.js:24); the delete handler discards it and sets the status on the next line (app.js:36). Driven in Playwright with Storage.prototype.setItem made to throw.
failing_case: Storage is full or blocked. User deletes a recipe and confirms. The status says 'Deleted “X”.', the row disappears, nothing was written. After a reload the recipe is back.
remediation: Use the boolean from saveRecipes in the delete handler. On failure show a message that says the change was not stored and how to fix it, as the add path already does. Do not show the success text.

title: Deleting a recipe destroys the focused Delete button and focus falls to <body>
evidence: The click handler calls render(), which replaces listEl.innerHTML (app.js:10). Driven: after confirming a delete, document.activeElement is BODY.
failing_case: A keyboard or screen-reader user tabs to the third Delete button and presses Enter. Focus is reset to the start of the page, so they must tab through the form again to reach the next recipe. This fails WCAG 2.4.3 (Focus Order, level A).
remediation: After removal, move focus to the next row's Delete button, or to the previous one, or to the list heading when the list is empty (add tabindex=-1 to it).

quote: return Array.isArray(data) ? data.filter((r) => r && typeof r.name === "string") : [];
title: loadRecipes checks only `name`; a record without a valid id or numeric minutes breaks delete and the total
evidence: Driven with localStorage = [{name:'Pie',minutes:30},{name:'Soup',minutes:'20',id:5}]. Delete on 'Pie' throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading name)' and no confirm dialog appears. The row renders data-id="undefined", so recipes.find(x => x.id === id) returns undefined and describe(undefined) throws; app.js:14 claims that can never happen. A numeric id (5) fails the strict string compare the same way. Adding 'Cake' (10) then shows 'Total cooking time: 302010 minutes.' because totalMinutes (store.js:23) concatenates the string '20'.
failing_case: A record saved by an older version, imported or hand-edited has no id, a numeric id, or minutes as a string. Its Delete button does nothing, with a console TypeError. The total shown after the next add is wrong ('302010 minutes' instead of 60).
remediation: Add one normaliser at the load boundary. Require a string id (assign one if missing), a finite number for minutes, and a string name, and drop or repair anything else. Make the delete handler tolerate find() returning undefined.

title: Delete throws on a stored record without a string id, so the row can never be removed
evidence: loadRecipes (store.js:7) keeps any record with a string name and checks nothing else. render escapes r.id into data-id (app.js:10), so a missing id becomes the string 'undefined' and a numeric id 123 becomes '123'. The handler matches with x.id === id (app.js:32). Strict equality fails, so r is undefined. describe(r) (app.js:15) reads recipe.name and throws TypeError. The comment at app.js:14 says recipe is never null. Traced.
failing_case: localStorage 'recipes' = [{"name":"Soup","minutes":20}] (an older shape with no id) or [{"id":1,"name":"Soup","minutes":20}]. The list renders. Clicking Delete throws in the click handler and nothing happens. The user cannot remove the item.
remediation: Normalise every record at load in one function. Assign a string id when it is missing and coerce it to a string when it is not, and coerce or default minutes. Guard the lookup with if (!r) return.

title: A long unbroken recipe name forces sideways scrolling at 390 px
evidence: The list item has no overflow-wrap or min-width rule. Driven at a 390 px viewport after saving an 80-character name (the maxlength) with no spaces: documentElement.scrollWidth is 624 against a clientWidth of 390.
failing_case: On a phone, a user saves 'aaaa...' of 80 characters, or a long URL-like name. The whole page scrolls sideways and the Delete button is off-screen. This fails WCAG 1.4.10 (Reflow, level AA).
remediation: Add `li { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }` and let the row wrap, for example with a flex row where the name has min-width:0.
